Vous interviendrez dans un environnement hybride : un socle historique en PHP que vous ferez évoluer progressivement vers un écosystème .NET Core, micro-services, Kubernetes et Linux.

Votre Journée Type :

Imaginez commencer votre journée par un café tout en analysant les derniers services déployés dans le cluster Kubernetes. Le ticketing interne vous présente les nouvelles demandes métiers : chacune nécessite une réflexion technique poussée, une capacité à construire un micro-service propre, robuste, scalable… et parfaitement intégré à l'architecture existante.

Vous échangez ensuite avec les donneurs d'ordre métier pour cadrer précisément les besoins. Votre rôle est essentiel : transformer un besoin fonctionnel en une solution technique pertinente, performante et durable.

Puis vous entrez dans votre zone de maîtrise :
Développement de micro-services .NET Core propres, découplés et maintenables.
Intégration dans un environnement Kubernetes / Linux (pods, services, observabilité, bonnes pratiques de résilience).
Manipulation et optimisation de données sous MS SQL.
Interaction avec l'héritage existant PHP, que vous comprenez suffisamment pour y interfacer ou en faire évoluer certaines briques.

Vous êtes force de proposition : vous challengez l'existant, proposez des améliorations, anticipez les impacts d'architecture. Votre pédagogie fait la différence : vous aimez transmettre vos bonnes pratiques aux autres développeurs pour améliorer la qualité globale du code.

En parallèle, la veille technologique est un réflexe naturel : patterns, bonnes pratiques de développement distribués, sécurité, performances… tout ce qui permet de faire évoluer nos services dans le bon sens.

Votre Mission :

  • Concevoir, développer et faire évoluer des micro-services .NET Core dans un environnement cloud-native basé sur Kubernetes, Linux, MS SQL et Git.
  • Interagir avec l'existant PHP lorsque nécessaire, en comprenant les enjeux techniques et les interfaces à maintenir.
  • Piloter vos développements de bout en bout : conception, documentation, qualité du code, tests, intégration et mise en production via des pipelines CI/CD.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes métier pour transformer les besoins en solutions techniques robustes et évolutives.
  • Être force de proposition sur l'architecture applicative : découpage en micro-services, patterns de communication, structuration du code, bonnes pratiques DevOps (sans être un profil infrastructure).
  • Transmettre vos bonnes pratiques de développement moderne (clean code, tests, observabilité, résilience) pour tirer l'équipe vers le haut.

Qui Êtes-Vous ?

Diplômé en informatique, vous affichez une solide expérience en développement back-end et full-stack .NET Core, dans des environnements distribués et orientés micro-services.
Votre maîtrise de .NET Core, des architectures découplées et des pratiques modernes de développement est votre véritable force.

À l'aise dans un écosystème Kubernetes / Linux, vous savez concevoir, déployer et maintenir des services robustes, scalables et observables.
Vous maîtrisez également MS SQL, indispensable pour manipuler et optimiser les données au cœur des processus métiers.

Vous avez déjà travaillé dans des environnements hybrides comprenant un héritage PHP, que vous savez appréhender ou interfacer au besoin - sans que ce soit votre principale spécialité.

Curieux, rigoureux et pédagogue, vous aimez transmettre vos bonnes pratiques de code à l'équipe, challenger l'existant et proposer des améliorations structurantes.
Vous êtes proactif, autonome, tout en appréciant travailler en coopération avec les équipes métier.

Une expérience dans le secteur bancaire est un plus, sans être obligatoire.

Pourquoi Le Crédit Agricole Île-de-France ?

Parce que vous rejoignez un environnement où innovation, architecture moderne et excellence technique se rencontrent pour transformer durablement le paysage financier.

Parce que vous prenez un rôle clé dans l'évolution des applications internes d'une grande banque régionale, avec un vrai impact technologique et une vision long terme.

Notre mission: être un partenaire de confiance pour chaque projet - qu'il s'agisse dedévelopper les territoires, soutenir les entreprises ou répondre aux besoinsessentiels des ménages - en mêlant innovation, expertise et proximité.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Interne Software weiterentwickeln. Du arbeitest dich in unsere bestehenden Anwendungen ein, setzt Änderungen im Code um und baust neue Frontends und Benutzeroberflächen mit No-Code- und Low-Code-Tools.

  • Geschäftsprozesse automatisieren. Du schaust dir an, welche Arbeitsschritte sich im Team wiederholen, und entwickelst dafür zuverlässige Workflows mit n8n, Make oder vergleichbaren Tools.

  • Technische Lösungen fürs Team umsetzen. Du klärst Anforderungen mit den Kollegen, führst bei Bedarf neue Tools ein und hilfst bei technischen Fragen zu unseren internen Systemen.

Das bringst du mit

  • 1-2 Jahre technisches Grundverständnis und praktische Programmiererfahrung. Du kannst dich in vorhandenen Code einarbeiten, Änderungen selbst umsetzen und Fehler systematisch eingrenzen. JavaScript oder TypeScript passen besonders gut zu unserem Stack. Andere Programmiersprachen wie Python sind ebenfalls eine gute Grundlage.

Job Description

Présentation du poste et de son contexte

Le service M&D (Monitoring & Diagnostic) a pour mission de collecter et d’analyser les données issues de nos machines installées sur site, afin d’apporter un support technique à nos clients. Ses activités se concentrent principalement sur le troubleshooting, la détection d’anomalies et l’amélioration de la performance et de la fiabilité des équipements.

Dans ce contexte, nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire ingénieur(e) pour contribuer au développement de solutions innovantes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle, ainsi qu’à l’automatisation et à l’optimisation de nos outils et processus quotidiens.

Principales missions et responsabilités

Le/la Stagiaire Sera Amené(e) à

  • Collaborer en binôme avec un développeur spécialisé en Intelligence Artificielle pour intégrer des solutions d’IA au sein d’une interface web ;
  • Tester, concevoir et développer des outils et solutions sur la plateforme APM/Predix ;
  • Proposer et développer des solutions innovantes pour automatiser les tâches quotidiennes et ponctuelles du service ;
  • Concevoir et développer des pipelines d’ingestion de données ;
  • Développer des API permettant la mise à disposition et l’exploitation des données ;
  • Participer à l’amélioration continue des outils de monitoring et de diagnostic.

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons un(e) étudiant(e) en école d’ingénieurs, avec une spécialisation en informatique, développement logiciel, data engineering ou intelligence artificielle.

Compétences techniques et comportementales requises

Compétences Techniques

  • Connaissances en bases de données SQL et NoSQL ;
  • Connaissances en réseaux informatiques ;
  • Maîtrise ou bonne connaissance des langages de programmation Python et JavaScript ;
  • Connaissances des technologies React, Node.js ou Next.js ;
  • Connaissances de FastAPI et Docker.

Compétences Comportementales

  • Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais ;
  • Esprit analytique et aisance avec les calculs ;
  • Autonomie et capacité à prendre des initiatives et des décisions ;
  • Esprit d’équipe et aptitude à collaborer efficacement ;
  • Curiosité technique et intérêt pour les nouvelles technologies.

Informations relatives au lieu de travail et à l’organisation

Le stage se déroulera sur notre site de Belfort (TE05), dans un environnement de travail collaboratif, avec des horaires de bureau standard.

Durée du stage : 6 mois.

Job Overview

The M&D (Monitoring & Diagnostics) department is responsible for collecting and analyzing data from our machines installed on-site, in order to provide technical support to our customers. Its main activities focus on troubleshooting, anomaly detection, and improving the performance and reliability of equipment.

In this context, we are looking for an Engineering Intern to contribute to the development of innovative solutions integrating Artificial Intelligence, as well as the automation and optimization of our daily tools and processes.

Key Responsibilities

The Intern Will Be Responsible For

  • Collaborating closely with an Artificial Intelligence developer to integrate AI solutions into a web interface;
  • Testing, designing, and developing tools and solutions on the APM/Predix platform;
  • Proposing and developing innovative solutions to automate daily and ad hoc tasks within the department;
  • Designing and developing data ingestion pipelines;
  • Developing APIs to enable data access and utilization;
  • Contributing to the continuous improvement of monitoring and diagnostic tools.

Required Qualifications

We are looking for an Engineering student specializing in Computer Science, Software Development, Data Engineering, or Artificial Intelligence.

Technical Skills

Required Technical and Behavioral Skills

  • Knowledge of SQL and NoSQL databases;
  • Knowledge of computer networking;
  • Proficiency in, or good knowledge of, Python and JavaScript programming languages;
  • Knowledge of React, Node.js, or Next.js;
  • Knowledge of FastAPI and Docker.

Behavioral Skills

  • Good command of English;
  • Strong analytical skills and numerical aptitude;
  • Autonomy and ability to take initiative and make decisions;
  • Team spirit and ability to collaborate effectively;
  • Technical curiosity and interest in emerging technologies.

Workplace and Organization

The internship will take place at our Belfort site (TE05), in a collaborative working environment, with standard office hours.

Internship Duration: 6 months.

GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE : GEV) est une entreprise mondiale dédiée au secteur de l'énergie, structurée autour de ses segments Power, Wind et Electrification, et soutenue par ses activités d'accélération. We are looking for an SAP Integration Architect to own how Finto connects to SAP. Some of our customers run their finance operations on SAP, and no two landscapes look alike: R/3, ECC and S/4HANA, on-premise and cloud, Business One and Business ByDesign. You'll design how master data, invoices and postings move between those systems and our AI platform, and turn what starts as a bespoke integration into a product that goes live in weeks. This is a hands-on role, working directly with our CTO and the founding team: you'll set the architecture, write code, and sit across the table from customer IT. You're the first hire dedicated to SAP at Finto and you define what the practice becomes. We're headquartered in Munich, with roots in San Francisco through Y Combinator.

What you'll do

  • Own the end-to-end architecture from a customer's SAP system into Finto: master data, invoices, postings, write-back.

  • Choose the integration path per SAP flavour - OData, IDoc, BAPI/RFC, BTP/CPI, file-based - and make that choice repeatable instead of re-deciding it per customer.

  • Build the connector platform: templates, validation, monitoring, and the tooling that makes every new landscape faster than the last.

  • Translate FI and MM process knowledge into specifications and field mappings our engineers build against.

  • Ship production code with the engineering team - same repo, same reviews, Node.js and TypeScript.

  • Be the SAP authority in the room: with customer IT, with their integration partners, and in our own technical conversations with prospects.

  • Set the standard for how Finto goes live on SAP, and move more of it into the product with every rollout.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of hands-on SAP integration work in real customer landscapes across R/3, ECC and S/4HANA, ideally more than one generation of them.

  • Deep knowledge of the accounts payable process in SAP: FI, MM, the document flow around incoming invoices, tax determination, and why the field a customer means is rarely the field the label says.

  • Fluency across SAP's integration surface - OData, IDocs, BAPI/RFC, BTP/CPI - and a clear position on clean core.

  • Strong coding skills, ideally in TypeScript/Node.js. You architect and you build; specifications alone aren't the job.

  • A product instinct: you'd rather build a pattern once than map the same fields twice.

  • Confidence in front of enterprise IT teams, and the directness to tell them when an export won't work.

  • Fluent German and English.

  • Bonus points for ABAP, for time on the consulting side of SAP rollouts, or for anything you've built that made your own job smaller.

  • An environment where we enable you to have an impact and where we focus on outcomes, not time-tracking.

Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

 

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

 

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

 

Rémunération : 75 000€ à 85 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 8 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

Role: Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff)

Company: CodeSpeak

Location: London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit.

Job Type: Full-time

About CodeSpeak

Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away.

CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years.

Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece.

CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift.

What you are expected to do:

Design and delivery

  • Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform.

  • Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result.

  • Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design.

  • Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team.

Product problems

CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it.

  • Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model.

  • In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review.

  • Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them.

  • Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open.

Ways of working

  • Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction.

  • Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences.

  • Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot.

  • Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard.

  • Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees.

What you need to succeed:

Craft

  • You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own.

  • You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical.

  • You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages.

  • You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software.

  • You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users.

How you work

  • You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here.

  • You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself.

  • You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools.

  • You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture.

  • You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered.

Nice to have

  • A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well.

  • Experience with complex data visualisation.

  • Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder.

A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this.

What you get:

  • An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks.

  • A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic.

  • An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists.

  • Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead.

  • Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years.

  • A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance.

  • Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you.

  • Work in AI, a field most people want to be in.

Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their

logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and

in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our

infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a

product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and

considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is

mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway

management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting

things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you

learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a

cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and

grow into the rest.

  • Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget
  • User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies, partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app
  • API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code
  • Payments and billing
  • ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging, observability and alerting, consent and retention
  • The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access
  • Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were never designed to meet

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want

someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and

used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and

Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is

TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity

layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How We Work

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around

agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,

the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the

implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What

we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand:

knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not

move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a

week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that

an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for

how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at

least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a

green build is never on its own enough to merge.

Requirements

You'll thrive here if you have...

  • Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to the machine they run on
  • A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for
  • Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's
  • React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters
  • TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types are carrying real weight
  • Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to pick up Pulumi
  • Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into
  • Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema change does under load
  • Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a colleague's
  • Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and patience for other people's undocumented edge cases
  • A working day that overlaps ours: based within CET ±3
  • Fluent in English, our working language

Nice to have

  • Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX
  • Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR beyond a cookie banner
  • Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations
  • Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent
  • Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry
  • Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU ETS..)

Benefits

Als Senior Electrical Engineer binnen onze Datacenter-afdeling ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerp, de engineering en de technische coördinatie van complexe elektrotechnische installaties. We hebben meegewerkt aan de bouw van diverse nieuwe datacenters in o.a. Milaan, Amsterdam. What we're building

Jiga is on a mission to help engineers build physical products faster. Think npm install for mechanical engineers - we're building the infrastructure that makes hardware development as fast as software.

How we actually work

We’re a small remote team made up of the best of the best. Our team members are distributed around the globe. While most of our product and engineering talent is located in Europe and Israel, you’ll also work with people from the US and Asia. Most of our work is made async, which is the secret sauce of our success.

  • High trust, low bullshit: We don't count hours or peek over your shoulder on Slack. We trust you to get your work done and tell us when something's wrong. You'll have real ownership over what you build: which means you'll make a lot of decisions about architecture and functionality without endless approval cycles. (If that sounds terrifying, we're probably not a good fit. If that sounds exciting, keep reading.)

  • Question everything: See something that doesn't make sense? Say it. Have a better way to do something? Just do it. We actually mean it when we say we want people to challenge the status quo and improve things. Our internal motto is “Don’t drink the kool-aid”

  • No stupid Meetings: One weekly all-hands. One dev team sync. That's literally it. Everything else happens async in Slack or Loom. Your calendar will be beautifully, gloriously empty.

  • Actually friendly, not corporate friendly: We play games online every week (current favorite: Make it Meme). Once a year we fly everyone somewhere beautiful for our offsite (Greece, here we come). We genuinely like hanging out together, which turns out to be way better than forced "team building exercises."

What we value in engineering:

Simple > Complicated. Simple code, simple architecture; Simple solutions are better than complex ones.

Ship it, then improve it. Perfection is the enemy of done. Launch now, iterate forever.

Product > Engineering. Every line of code should make our users' lives better. We're not here to show off our algorithmic prowess - we're here to solve real business problems.

Financials

Jiga is fully funded, cashflow positive, with growing revenue MoM. We're completely transparent about our runway and finances - ask us anything.

You'll love it here if

  • You want to actually own things. Not "ownership" where you need three approvals to change a button color. Real ownership where you decide what to build, how to build it, and when to ship it.

  • You're genuinely full-stack - you're equally happy building a slick UI component or optimizing a database query. There's no task you'd refuse because it's "not your specialty."

  • You care about the product, not just the code. You want to understand why we're building something and you'll push back if it doesn't make sense.

  • You are motivated to run a marathon and ring the bell with us in 3-4 years from now.

  • Bureaucracy makes you want to scream. Multiple approval layers, process for the sake of process, corporate theatre - if these sound like your nightmare, welcome home.

  • You love shipping. Like, you get genuinely excited when you push to production. That "it's alive!" feeling never gets old.

  • You work fast because you're having fun, not because someone's watching you.

This might not be for you if

  • You hate ambiguity. You prefer clear, detailed task assignments and well-defined requirements

  • You like having management to check in, review and verify your work multiple times until it’s perfect

  • You're looking for a cuddly, 9-5, corporate job where you can coast a bit

  • You like the smell of gasoline and motor oil while driving to the office every day (sorry, we are 100% remote)

  • You like weeks of architecting over-complicated solutions

(No judgment if that's what you want - it's just not what we are.)

What you need

  • 3+ years building full-stack web applications end-to-end

  • Strong at React + Node.js. MongoDB experience is a great plus.

  • Experience building complex applications - you understand clean architecture, security, scaling, performance, and maintainability

  • Solid data modeling fundamentals

  • Product company experience (you've felt the joy and pain of real users)

  • Some overlap with GMT+3 working hours so we can actually talk to you sometimes

What we offer

No ping pong tables. No beer kegs. No "unlimited vacation" that nobody takes. No ice cream fridge at the office. Oh right, we don't even have an office.

Here's what we do have:

  • A small team where you matter - we never compromise on people, that means you are part of the best team in the world.

  • Zero bureaucracy - we hate process theatre as much as you do

  • Real ownership and responsibility - make decisions, ship code, own the outcomes. Have real impact on the product from day 1.

  • Complete flexibility - work from anywhere, set your own hours, take time off when you need it (parents and DMs are very welcome)

  • Genuinely high trust - we trust you to do great work and be honest when things go sideways

  • A team that actually likes each other - international, diverse, genuinely friendly people who enjoy working together

  • Generous stock options - we’re looking for partners to run a marathon with us, you will get a life-changing shares when we get to the finish line

  • Competitive salary and PTOs - so you can also enjoy, relax and recharge

  • Self-development budget for books, courses, conferences, whatever helps you grow

  • Annual offsite in beautiful places (greece, here we come!)

  • Fast-paced environment with tons of creative freedom

  • Hard, interesting problems with a team that's positioned to win big

How to apply:

Send us a short blurb about yourself and your favorite ice cream flavor. (Mine's cookies. Please don’t write “Vanilla JS” 😒 )

  • 🌐 Proven Product Market Fit: Jus Mundi has achieved product-market fit in global markets since launch, partnering with top-tier law firms, government bodies, and major corporations, including Freshfields, Quinn Emanuel, Wong Partnership, TotalEnergies, and public institutions in Canada, the United Kingdom, and Japan.
  • 💸 Strategic Investment: We recently raised over $20 million in Series B funding from prominent strategic international investors, including Acton Capital, True Global Ventures, C4 Ventures, and FJ Labs, fueling our growth and innovation.
  • 🤖 Legal Meets Tech: Our engineers and former lawyers collaborate closely with large language models (LLMs) to pioneer the future of generative AI and reshape professional services.
  • 🌟 Exceptional Team: Work with talented professionals from industry leaders, including engineers, legal experts, and AI specialists from companies like Google and Amazon who are pushing the boundaries of legal tech.


📌 About the Role


Jus Mundi is building the AI layer for international law and arbitration — turning a vast, multilingual corpus of case law, treaties, and legal analysis into answers practitioners can trust. We are now expanding beyond arbitration into new legal verticals, and each one potentially adds millions of documents to that corpus.


To support that, we are building a new Data Platform: an autonomous, agent-driven system that discovers, acquires, processes and enriches legal documents end to end, and becomes the company-wide source of truth that Search, AI and Product all consume. It replaces our legacy ingestion paths rather than patching them.


We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer with hands-on AI experience to build it with us. You will own the services behind the platform: the agents that acquire documents from hundreds of heterogeneous sources, the transactional catalog and API that everything reads from, and the processing layer that turns raw files into searchable, well-described documents.


This is a hands-on senior role with high ownership and real architectural latitude. Backend depth is the core of the role; you should be comfortable working with LLMs and agent orchestration as a first-class part of the system, but this is not a modelling or research position.



🙌 The Team


You will join the Data team within EPD (Engineering, Product and Design) — a small, senior team made up of an Engineering Manager, a backend/full-stack engineer, and an AI engineer reinforcing us over the coming months.


We work in close collaboration with the Legal Content team, who own what “correct” means for a legal document, and with the Search, AI and Product squads who consume what the platform produces.


🌟Your mission at Jus Mundi


  • Agentic ingestion (core of this role): Build the agents that acquire documents from hundreds of heterogeneous sources — the orchestration loop, tool calling, memory, and the guarantees that make a sweep provably complete rather than approximately complete.
  • Backend services and data model (core of this role): Own the transactional catalog and the API in front of it — the single door to the platform’s data. Design a schema that holds heterogeneous, evolving legal documents with provenance and confidence on every field, and that absorbs new contributors without a migration.
  • Document processing: Extraction, OCR and metadata over a messy multilingual corpus.
  • Derived data stays versioned and regenerable, so a better model means a re-run rather than a re-acquisition.
  • Quality without manual gates: We deliberately have no human approval step before a document becomes searchable, so quality has to be measured. Test sets, thresholds, confidence and regression tracking are how a component earns its way into production. We will develop Human-In-the-Loop architecture
  • Run what you build: Deploy, instrument and operate your own services. Metrics, logs and traces that let anyone reconstruct a single document’s whole history from one identifier.
  • Leverage across squads: Search, AI and Product all build on this platform. You design the stable interfaces they consume, write the RFCs that get decisions validated, and help us grow the team.

Scope will move as the platform does — this is an early-stage system, and we would rather you help shape the roadmap than inherit it.


⚙️ Preferred Experience and Skills


  • Backend Engineering Depth (critical requirement): 5+ years shipping and operating production backend or data services, with strong Python . Async I/O, API design, testing discipline, and a track record of owning services in production rather than handing them over.
  • Agentic & LLM Systems (critical requirement): Hands-on experience building agent orchestration in production — tool/function calling, memory and state management, error recovery, bounded context, and deterministic contracts wrapped around a non-deterministic core. Custom architecture or a framework (LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar) are equally welcome; what matters is that you can point at something you shipped and had to keep working.
  • Data Modelling: Postgres in depth — schema design for heterogeneous and evolving data, jsonb versus typed columns, indexing, full-text search, migrations under load, and a real feel for transactional correctness.
  • Systems Judgment: Queues or streams, idempotency, at-least-once semantics, atomic writes, object storage treated as immutable truth. You design for retry, reproducibility and graceful degradation rather than assuming the happy path.
  • Document & Data Processing: PDF and HTML text extraction, OCR, and structured metadata extraction with LLMs — plus realistic judgement about where quality breaks and what that costs downstream. Multilingual corpora a strong plus.
  • Ownership & DevOps Mentality: Containers, CI/CD, Kubernetes or equivalent. You build it, you run it, you own it — including when it pages.
  • Senior Behaviours: Turns ambiguity into a plan and a document others can act on; makes explicit trade-offs rather than reaching for the perfect solution; mentors peers; takes
  • accountability for outcomes. Fluent English (our working language, oral and written).


Nice to Have


  • Web crawling and scraping at scale — pagination traps, rendering, rate limits, source drift, dedup. We are taking an agentic-first approach, so this is a real bonus rather than a requirement.
  • Legal tech, or another domain where being confidently wrong is expensive.
  • Search infrastructure (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch) and multilingual retrieval.
  • Enough TypeScript/JS to contribute to our internal back-office UI.
  • Experience with the MCP ecosystem, or agent tooling you built yourself.
  • Open-source contributions, or a portfolio of systems you can talk through in depth


🔄 Interview process


We’re proud of our multicultural team representing 37 nationalities! To ensure smooth communication, please apply in English (CV and application form questions).

  • Last call with Jean-Rémi, CEO, or Anna, VP of People (30 min)


Please note that, due to the nature of the sector we operate in, the final steps of our recruitment process include reference calls and a background check.


Need More Reasons to Join Us? ✨


  • 💻 Enjoy a hybrid working organization that combines remote and on-site work (2 days).
  • 🏖 Get 5 weeks of vacation each year, and take them whenever it suits you.
  • 🩺 Receive 100% coverage of private health insurance for yourself and your children.

L'équipe produit d'Ecair se structure autour de ses Product Engineers. Pour qu'ils soient le plus productif possible et le mieux accompagné, nous créons une équipe "plateforme" au sein de l'équipe Engineering.

Ce rôle est le premier de cet équipe, et

Perspectives

Vous rejoindrez l'équipe produit d'Ecair à un moment excitant : quelques uns de nos produits ont fait leurs preuves, mais tout reste à construire et à consolider.

Il y a notamment beaucoup de travail sur :

  • notre plateforme agentique qui automatise notre traitement des dossiers pour plus de sécurité, de rapidité et d'efficacité pour nos clients.

  • nos offres de financement des particuliers, le premier impact au quotidien sur la transition écologique.

Product Stack

L'équipe suit le modèle pragmatique proposé par Linear : cycles de deux semaines et projets qui correspondent à de grandes ou petites initiatives. Deux PMs sont attendus dans les prochains mois pour nous aider à mieux gérer les priorités et la définition des besoins.

Nos équipes opérationnelles utilisent la même web app que nos clients et que les particuliers, cela nous permets d'avoir une écoute et une réactivité très forte sur la qualité de nos produits.

Engineering

Petite sélections de principes représentatifs de notre pratique :

  • Nous pensons qu'il n'y pas d'exclusivité entre la vélocité et la rigueur.

  • Nous n'avons pas besoin d'être rapides (nous ne sommes pas à 5ms près) - ce qui ne nous autorise pas à être lents (p95 <600ms), mais nous permets de privilégier la qualité de lecture et de modélisation des problèmes que nous rencontrons.

  • Typescript est un outil formidable et très expressif. Nous l'utilisons pleinement et c'est notre premier outil de travail.

  • Nous n'avons pas de passion pour nos outils, nous choisissons ceux qui répondent le mieux à nos problèmes.

Tech Stack

Les produits Ecair sont distribués via une web app React (Vite SPA, Tailwind, Cloudflare) et une API publique pour nos partenaires (OpenAPI, Hono).

Nos backends sont des systèmes distribués : notre API HTTP interne opère avec tRPC, PostgreSQL (DrizzleORM), S3 et Redis, notre asynchrone sont opérés avec Redis et BullMQ.

Le monitoring est fait avec Datadog (logs, APM, error management).

Coding Agents

Approche enthousiaste mais rigoureuse. L'équipe tourne majoritairement sur les modèles Anthropic, et expérimente à un rythme en adéquation avec son mandat principal (construire le financement de la transition écologique). Réunions régulières pour échanger sur le sujet.

Depuis le début de 2026, 26% de nos PRs ont été shippées entièrement par Claude, et Claude a été impliqué dans au moins 50% du reste.

La direction que nous allons suivre consistera à renforcer encore nos usages Typescript et linters pour faciliter la tâche aux agents au maximum.

6 ans minimum dans un rôle de Software Engineer ou Product Engineer, dans un environnement orienté produit et tech, et dans des rôles "plateforme" pour l'engineering.

  • Remote, 30min : discussion initiale et screening technique Typescript avec Julien, notre recruteur

  • Remote, 30min : discussion ouverte sur le software engineering avec Théo, notre CTO

  • Async, 1h30 : homework "écriture technique", rédaction d'un document technique dans un usecase bien précis.

  • Remote, 2h30 : trois tech interviews avec deux pauses de 15 minutes ; 45 minutes de React+Typescript, puis 30 minutes de code review, et 30 minutes de system design

  • Onsite d'une demie journée pour rencontrer les fondateurs et l'équipe produit.

Les Nouvelles Recrues is hiring on behalf of our client Fabriq

1. Our client, its business and its ambition

The ambition. Our client Fabriq is bringing European industry into the 21st century: making factories more competitive and frontline teams more autonomous. This is not only a software play, it is the industrial relocalisation project.

The business. Fabriq is the SaaS platform that replaces the whiteboards and Excel spreadsheets still running 80% of industrial sites. Operators, team leads and plant managers track real-time KPIs (safety, quality, lead time, productivity), surface and solve shop-floor problems, run their daily routines and collaborate across teams in one place. Fabriq's long-term ambition is to become the Operating System of every production floor.

The proof.

  • 700+ industrial sites equipped across 43+ countries.

  • Reference customers such as Safran, Airbus, Renault, Scania, LVMH, Andros, Bel, Merck and Lonza.

  • Profitable since late 2024, then €22M raised in June 2025 with Expedition Capital to accelerate in the US, the UK and DACH.

  • A team of ~140 people, and an AI roadmap that is already in customers' hands rather than on a slide.

2. The role

Context: You join Fabriq's AI team, currently a three-person unit led by Jean (Product Lead) alongside two Senior Engineers: Halim & Rafik. This team operates as a prototyping squad at the front edge of the company: it tests new ideas, measures market appetite and decides whether Fabriq goes there. Products are in alpha, cycles are short, the roadmap is directional. The team also works weekly with Octave, co-founder, which gives you direct exposure to the strategic decisions.

Objective: Become the third engineer on AI alongside Halim and Rafik, reach full autonomy on the stack and the customer context within 6 months, and take Fabriq's AI products from alpha to something industrial teams rely on every day.

Challenges:

  • Taking AI prototypes to production quality. Conversational and voice-driven agents, plugged into real industrial data and used by real teams on the floor. You take them from alpha to something people rely on daily: answer quality, reliability, and the cost per interaction that decides whether a use case scales or gets dropped.

  • Prototyping to convince. Part of the roadmap is co-built with partner customers, which means it is sold before it is built. Specs move as customers shape them, timelines are tight, and you build fast to prove a use case is worth pursuing. Testing a lot and abandoning a lot is part of the deal.

  • Agentic engineering from scratch. No Mastra, no LangGraph, no off-the-shelf framework. Everything is hand-built in TypeScript and Deno on top of frontier models called through AWS Bedrock. When the team needs something like agent memory compaction, you design it yourself. This is custom, sparsely documented territory, and that is precisely the technical interest of the role.

  • Setting the technical direction with Halim and Rafik. You are the third engineer, not an extra pair of hands: code reviews, architecture debates, and the freedom to arrive with your own proposals rather than waiting for a ticket.

Your first 3 months are dedicated to ramping up on the Fabriq stack and product, contributing to the AI features already in the hands of beta customers, and shipping your first POCs.

3. Skills and experience

Must-haves:

  • Software engineering depth: 4 to 5 years minimum. Real craftsmanship, clean design decisions, and the ability to explain the architecture trade-offs you made and why.

  • Daily hands-on use of AI to build software. Having never used AI to develop is a deal-breaker on this role.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You move forward, decide and ship when nothing is specified in advance, and you adapt when the roadmap shifts.

  • Builder mindset with evidence. Concrete examples of things you built from zero, prototyped, tested and iterated on.

Nice-to-haves (optional):

  • A first hands-on experience with agentic systems. Expertise is welcome when it is real: a strong engineer with curiosity and early agentic work beats a self-declared two-year agentic expert who cannot explain concretely what they built.

  • A data background. The testing logic differs from pure software: working on datasets and analysing where a system succeeds and where it fails is a plus, and it can be learned at Fabriq.

  • Collaborative posture. The team will evangelise AI across the other product teams. Showing and explaining your work is expected.

Stack:
Backend: TypeScript on Deno. Frontend: Vue.js. Infrastructure: AWS with EKS, Terraform, plus Kubernetes for on-prem customer deployments. Observability: Honeycomb and Sentry. On the AI side: frontier models called through AWS Bedrock, with everything agentic hand-built and no framework on top.

4. Package and working conditions

  • Salary: €70K to €80K fixed, depending on experience.

  • Location: Fabriq's Paris office at 18 rue Yves Toudic, 75010. Presence matters most during onboarding and for team dynamics. Remote is possible, Paris is preferred.

  • Working language: French & English, fluency required.

  • Benefits: 7 weeks of vacation per year, Alan health insurance, Swile meal vouchers, a company event every quarter and an annual offsite.

Hiring process:

  1. Screening call with Les Nouvelles Recrues, Fabriq's recruitment partner: 30 to 45 min

  2. Technical interview with a Fabriq technical profile: 1h45 (project review, system design and product mindset, technical Q&A)

  3. Team fit with Jean, Halim & Rafik : 1h

  4. Reference checks: 2 references

  5. Meeting with Octave, Fabriq co-founder: 30 min

Dans le cadre du développement de solutions de démonstration et de validation de systèmes embarqués connectés, l'equipe IoT Sensors souhaite mettre en place une plateforme Web permettant de simplifier l'appairage de capteurs Zigbee Green Power, de collecter les données qu'ils transmettent et de les visualiser en temps réel à travers une interface utilisateur moderne et intuitive.

Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About North:

North is Cohere's cutting-edge AI workspace platform, designed to revolutionize the way enterprises utilize AI. It offers a secure and customizable environment, allowing companies to deploy AI while maintaining control over sensitive data. North integrates seamlessly with existing workflows, providing a trusted platform that connects AI agents with workplace tools and applications.

Why This Role?

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how enterprises harness the power of AI in real-world applications. As a bridge between our core North product and our clients’ engineering teams, you’ll be at the forefront of solving complex problems and securely integrating AI into critical sectors such as finance, healthcare, and telecommunications.

We’re looking for Software Engineers with Applied AI experience who can own the design, build, and deployment of agentic workflows powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), from early prototypes to production-grade AI agents, to deliver concrete business value in enterprise workflows.

You’ll work closely with customers on real-world business problems, often building first-of-their-kind agent workflows that integrate LLMs with tools, APIs, and data sources. While our pace is startup-fast, the bar is enterprise-high: agents must be reliable, observable, safe, and auditable from day one.

In this role, you will:

  • Work closely with our enterprise customers to translate high-value, ambiguous business problems into well-framed agentic workflows with clear success criteria and evaluation methodologies

  • Lead the design, build, and delivery of LLM-powered agents that reason, plan, and act across tools, APIs, and sensitive enterprise data sources, with enterprise-grade reliability and performance

  • Build and ship features for North, our AI workspace platform, working across the full product lifecycle from conceptualisation through production

  • Take ownership of scoping and shaping use cases end-to-end, flexing into whatever technical area the problem demands (including frontend) to drive the most effective solution

  • Contribute to shared frameworks and patterns that enable consistent, high-quality delivery across customers and teams

  • Drive clarity in ambiguous situations, build alignment, and raise engineering quality across the organization

  • Travel up to 20–40% to work on-site with customers and partners

You may be a good fit if:

  • You have hands-on experience building and deploying production-grade software in Python; you write clean, testable, observable, scalable code

  • You've built and deployed highly performant RAG and agentic applications, including agents that plan and execute multi-step tasks using patterns like ReAct or Plan-and-Execute

  • You're deeply familiar with the LLM stack: frontier models, vector databases, and orchestration frameworks

  • You have a proven ability to build robust evaluation frameworks, moving well beyond trial and error, to measure agent accuracy, safety, and latency

  • You’re experienced working directly with customers and can lead technical discussions with enterprise stakeholders, translating ambiguous business needs into concrete technical specs

  • You have experience owning the full scope of a use case end-to-end

  • You thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments and can execute well even when priorities are shifting

It's a bonus if you have:

  • Experience setting architectural standards for AI and agentic systems across distributed teams

  • Experience flexing into unfamiliar technical areas, such as frontend, when the problem calls for it

  • Exposure to regulated or sensitive industry environments (finance, healthcare, telecoms)

  • Experience with enterprise security, compliance, or auditability requirements for AI systems

Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks:

  • A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

  • Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

  • RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

  • 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

  • Annual enrichment benefits:

    Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

    Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

  • 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

  • Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How and Where We Work:

  • Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

  • For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

  • For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

  • Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès
Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean.
 
Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA.

Ton équipe :
Tu rejoindras une communauté tech de plus de 120 Theodoers : software engineers, tech leads, engineering managers et architectes, avec lesquels tu pourras échanger, apprendre et progresser au quotidien.
 
Chez Theodo, les techs travaillent en équipes projet, constituées en fonction des besoins de chaque client. Tu feras partie d’une équipe de Theodoers à taille humaine (4 à 5 personnes), réunissant Software Engineers, Tech Lead et Product Manager. Ensemble, vous collaborerez étroitement avec le client, avec des échanges réguliers pour partager vos avancées, approfondir la compréhension de son problème et faire évoluer le produit au plus près des besoins de ses utilisateurs.
 
Tes futures missions :
En tant que Software Engineer Fullstack chez Theodo, ta mission sera de concevoir et développer des produits digitaux utiles, performants et durables pour répondre aux problématiques de nos clients et de leurs utilisateurs.
 
Tout au long de tes projets, tu seras accompagné pour monter en compétences et apprendre à écrire du code de qualité, à comprendre les enjeux produit et à intervenir sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie d’une application, de la conception au déploiement.
 
Tes futures missions en tant que Software Engineer chez Theodo :
  • Comprendre le problème de ton client et y répondre avec un produit performant, maintenable et orienté valeur, en intervenant sur tout le cycle de production, de la conception au déploiement.
  • Produire du code de qualité dans les délais, en intégrant tests, refactoring et standards techniques de l’équipe, quelle que soit la technologie utilisée.
  • Mener des investigations techniques, débugger efficacement et corriger les défauts de manière pérenne, dans tout type d’environnement.
  • Analyser en profondeur des problèmes dans le code pour développer son esprit de résolution de problèmes
  • Travailler avec un LLM pour accélérer les développements
 
Les problématiques et les technos sont très différentes d’un projet à l’autre, voici quelques exemples :
  • iDealwine® : leader mondial des enchères de vins en ligne a engagé la migration de son site e-commerce monolithique vers une architecture composable pour gagner en évolutivité, en sécurité et en maîtrise technologique. Après 2 mois de cadrage, les équipes Theodo ont piloté une approche design-to-cost permettant de modulariser la plateforme et de migrer 20 ans d’historique en 14 mois, dans le respect du budget et du planning.
  • Sevetys : refonte complète d’une web app métier avec deux volets stratégiques : un outil de prise de rendez-vous pour les propriétaires d’animaux et un back-office dédié aux vétérinaires. Deux équipes produit ont piloté la reconstruction des plateformes de bout en bout, rejointes en fin de projet par une équipe data pour structurer et valoriser les données. Principal défi : une mise en production coordonnée à grande échelle, impliquant de nombreuses cliniques vétérinaires, sans interruption d’activité.
Parmi les technos les plus représentées sur nos projets, tu pourras être amené à travailler avec : Java (Spring Boot), Angular, Node (Nest), React (Next), Python… 
 
Tes perspectives d'évolution :
Notre ambition est de former les leaders de la tech de demain. Grâce au coaching et formations que l’on propose, tu pourras :
  • Devenir un expert en développement en étant formé aux meilleurs standards de qualité
  • Développer des compétences transverses : coaching, recrutement, commercial, management et marketing technique
  • Participer à des groupes d’expertises avec d’autres passionnés (Cybersécurité, Serverless, Performance, GreenIT…)
  • Construire ton parcours sur-mesure pour atteindre tes objectifs : tech lead, senior architecte, évangéliste (spécialiste d’un sujet), CTO ou fondateur d’une entité etc
 
Une méthodologie basée sur l’apprentissage continu :
Chez Theodo, nous avons construit notre approche tech autour d’une conviction forte : on développe d’abord les personnes, avant de développer les produits.
 
Notre Lean Tech® System met l’accent sur l’apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l’objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour, tout en construisant des produits utiles et performants pour nos clients.
 
Profil recherché :
Nous recherchons avant tout des potentiels plus que des compétences déjà acquises. Si tu n’es pas encore un·e développeur·se chevronné·e, ce n’est pas un frein : ne te retiens pas pour postuler.
 
  • Tu es diplômé·e d’une top école d’ingénieur
  • Tu aimes travailler en équipe et intéragir avec des profils et des métiers variés, en faisant preuve de pédagogie et d’esprit constructif (revues de code, pair programming)
  • Tu es orienté·e création de valeur : tu t’intéresses à l’activité du client et tu ne fais pas de la tech pour la tech
  • Tu es promoteur de l’IA, notamment sur les sujets de GenAI, et tu cherches à progresser en continu grâce à la veille technique
  • Tu fais preuve d’exigence sur la qualité du travail produit et sais questionner, voire interrompre, la chaîne de production lorsque nécessaire (#jidoka)
  • Tu aimes travailler de manière structurée et appliques naturellement des principes d’organisation et d’amélioration continue (inspirés du 5S)
  • Tu souhaites évoluer dans un environnement qui encourage au quotidien l’envie de progresser, l’esprit d’équipe et la prise d’initiative
 
Le processus de recrutement :
  • Un premier call de 30 minutes avec un recruteur
  • Un échange d’une heure avec le même recruteur
  • Un exercice de refactoring à effectuer chez toi, suivi d’un échange avec un tech lead pour revenir sur tes erreurs
  • Un exercice en direct de debuging
  • Un entretien dirigeant de 30 minutes pour revenir sur tes motivations à rejoindre Theodo et répondre à tes derniers questions
Pourquoi rejoindre Theodo ?
L’environnement:
💼 Rejoindre un groupe de 750 personnes avec de nombreuses possibilités d’évolutions cross-entités
🤝  Chaque Theodoer est accompagné par un coach interne. Son objectif : t’épauler dans ton quotidien et parler objectifs de carrière via des séances de coaching hebdomadaires.
🎯 Participation à des projets associatifs grâce à la Fondation Theodo (Ada Tech School, Code Phoenix, Article 1…)
🎉 Soirées mensuelles, keynotes et week-end d’entreprise annuel
